overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. The law does not require public comment, and the chair has discretion over whether and how to permit it, so the factual dispute over the calls was not resolved.

allegations.summary: Mayor allegedly muted herself during public input while screening calls, then unmuted and let callers speak, at January and February meetings.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body allow public participation in a meeting.

allegations.summary: Calls from the public went unanswered at the January 26 and February 16 meetings; the February 16 meeting proceeded with no public comment despite many callers trying to dial in.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Council was not required by the Open Meeting Law to include a public comment period during its meetings at all, we do not herein resolve the factual dispute regarding whether any, or how many, callers were permitted to offer comment during the January and February meetings.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
